teaser: Most purchases are bets on future value; a reading balance that can go negative asks for payment when the value is already in view.
core_idea: Subscriptions, gym memberships and annual donations ask people to pay at the moment of most doubt for value that may not arrive, and research shows they often overpay and keep paying; this newsroom's meter reverses it with a £5 credit that reading draws down, prices the reader can lower or refuse, and a balance allowed to go negative, so payment arrives when accumulated value is visible, which works only where serving costs almost nothing and value adds up visibly, and could be made fairer with prices by purchasing power and a view of where the money goes, tested against written hypotheses with a December review.
